title: The proclamation and command
summary: Mosiah issues a proclamation against persecution. The churches are commanded to prohibit persecution, maintain equality, reject pride, esteem neighbors, and support themselves by labor; priests and teachers also work except when sick or in great want.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah sends a proclamation throughout the land that unbelievers should not persecute members of the church.
The churches are commanded to have no persecutions among them and to maintain equality among all men.
They are commanded not to let pride or haughtiness disturb their peace, to esteem neighbors as themselves, and to labor for their support.
Priests and teachers are to labor for their support, except in sickness or great want.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A proclamation being issued or read is a reasonable way to visualize the decree.
unspecified_visual_details: The proclamation's physical form, its reader, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there should not any unbeliever persecute any of those who belonged to the church of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The commands are reported, not a separately narrated public gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a public announcement scene, exact wording beyond quoted source text, or a specific labor task.

title: Peace and growth in the land
summary: Priests and teachers should labor for their own support except in sickness or much want; doing these things, they abound in the grace of God. Peace begins again, and the people grow numerous and spread in all directions, building large cities and villages. The Lord visits and prospers them, and they become a large and wealthy people.

explicit_facts.text: Priests and teachers should labor with their own hands for their support, except in sickness or much want; doing these things, they abound in the grace of God.
Much peace begins again in the land; the people become numerous and spread north, south, east, and west, building large cities and villages throughout the land.
The Lord visits and prospers them, and they become a large and wealthy people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A non-dramatized landscape illustration may accompany the narration without staging the reported developments as simultaneous actions.
unspecified_visual_details: The land's name and geographic features.
The people's appearance and clothing.

narration.text: Yea, and all their priests and teachers should labor with their own hands for their support, in all cases save it were in sickness, or in much want;
And there began to be much peace again in the land;
And the Lord did visit them and prosper them, and they became a large and wealthy people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses summarize developments over time rather than establish a single immediate event.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the land as Zarahemla or assign other geographic names.
Do not stage the reported labor, expansion, construction, and prosperity as a new present-tense event or compress them into one moment.
Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord.

He speaks as it were with a voice of thunder, causing the earth beneath them to shake. They fall to the earth in astonishment and do not understand his words.

The passage teaches that they become new creatures and otherwise cannot inherit the kingdom of God.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s appearance, clothing, posture, and surroundings are unspecified.
No audience is specified.
